text: A Banquet for Seaweed, by Haidar Haidar, was withdrawn from sale in Egypt in 2000. In April 2000 the Islamist newspaper al-Sh`ab campaigned against the Ministry of Culture's reprinting of the book; its article and al-Azhar's Islamic Research Council claimed it was blasphemous, lacked the council's legally required approval, and should be banned. Egypt's culture minister announced that the book had been withdrawn from sale pending an investigation of its contents, and the parliament's Religious Affairs Committee demanded that it be burned in public. The Grand Sheikh of al-Azhar, who is government-appointed, said that it deserved to be banned.
meta_description: A Banquet for Seaweed by Haidar Haidar was withdrawn from sale in Egypt in 2000 after an Islamist campaign; the Grand Sheikh of al-Azhar said it deserved a ban.
